items.stem: Why does a relational database read and write data in fixed-size pages rather than individual rows from disk?

options.text: Disk and OS I/O operate efficiently on blocks, so page-level I/O amortises the cost of access
options.rationale: Correct: block-oriented I/O makes per-row disk access wasteful; pages batch many rows per transfer and fit the buffer pool.

options.text: Rows cannot be addressed individually in any database
options.rationale: Rows are addressable logically; the page is the physical I/O unit for efficiency.
Paging is about I/O efficiency, not encryption.

options.text: It removes the need for indexes
options.rationale: Paging does not replace indexes; both serve different roles.

items.explanation: Correct: block-oriented I/O makes per-row disk access wasteful; pages batch many rows per transfer and fit the buffer pool.

items.stem: Which statements about B+-tree indexes are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: They keep keys sorted, so they support range scans efficiently
options.rationale: Correct: ordered leaves let a B+-tree serve range queries as well as point lookups.

options.text: Each extra index adds write and storage overhead
options.rationale: Correct: every index must be maintained on insert/update, so indexing everything hurts writes.

options.text: A B+-tree gives constant-time lookup independent of size
options.rationale: Lookup is logarithmic in the number of keys, not constant.

options.text: B+-trees cannot be used as a clustered index
options.rationale: Clustered indexes are commonly implemented as B+-trees.

items.explanation: Correct: ordered leaves let a B+-tree serve range queries as well as point lookups.; Correct: every index must be maintained on insert/update, so indexing everything hurts writes.

items.stem: Which isolation level prevents dirty reads but still allows non-repeatable reads?

options.rationale: Correct: Read Committed blocks dirty reads but permits non-repeatable reads and phantoms.
Read Uncommitted allows dirty reads, so it does not prevent them.
Serializable prevents non-repeatable reads and phantoms as well, so it is stricter than asked.

options.text: No isolation level prevents dirty reads
options.rationale: Read Committed and higher prevent dirty reads.

items.explanation: Correct: Read Committed blocks dirty reads but permits non-repeatable reads and phantoms.
